paragraphs: Chasa. (Son of Yedutun, and Chosah, among the gatekeepers; I Chronicles 16:38 [the source here gives פט״ז-לב, 16:32; a biblical name parallel, not an identification].) In Ketubot 85b: A certain man deposited a silver cup with Chasa; Chasa died without having given instructions about it. Rav Nachman said: I know Chasa, that he was not wealthy. And Rashi explains that he is the Chasa mentioned in Yevamot 121b who drowned in the river, and Rav Nachman said: By God, the fish have eaten Chasa; his wife went and remarried. Some say Rav Nachman ruled for her that she is permitted to remarry, since he said: Chasa was a great man; if he had emerged [from the river], word would have got around. And in Bava Metzia 57a we find: Rava said in the name of Rav Chasa: Rabbi Ami asked — Rav Nachman said: Rav Chasa later said that Rabbi Ami resolved it.
And in Dikdukei Soferim the reading is Chasa without the title Rav, and perhaps he is the Chasa mentioned above.
And we find in Shabbat 88a: Chasa bar Dacha [printed: דכא]. And in Bava Metzia 86a: Rav Chasa the son of the daughter of Chasa.

notes.text: The source text here gives I Chronicles 16:32; the quoted biblical words occur at 16:38. This is a biblical name parallel, not an identification of the later Chasa. The drowning account gives alternate versions of the widow’s remarriage.

Yevamot 121b gives both the widow’s remarriage after overhearing and the alternate report of Nachman explicitly permitting it. The latter is followed by a rejection of initial permission; reporting the variant is not endorsing that permission as the final rule.
